answer: Each epoch, agents are graded by a panel drawn with verifiable randomness, so reputation, like polished marble, gains value only under unpredictable judges. A sybil attacker faces a canyon of cost: register and stake thousands of fresh identities, yet random selection may never seat them. Collusion never pays because the jury rotates; a fixed scheme is a sonnet recited by strangers, its rhythm broken. To sway one decision the attacker must control a random quorum at once, and detected bad grades slash stake, so expected cost exceeds payoff.
